question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in global `tools.exec.pty` default for shell exec calls, and what guardrails must ship with it?
rationale: The request is a new shell-exec config/default surface, and repository policy treats config defaults plus exec behavior as security and compatibility sensitive.

options.title: Approve Guarded Opt-In
options.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` with default `false`, per-call override precedence, direct/gateway coverage, docs/help, regression tests, and sandbox warning coordination.

options.title: Reject Global Default
options.body: Keep PTY as a per-call model/tool parameter and ask users to rely on skills or explicit tool calls instead of adding another exec config knob.

options.title: Defer For Sandbox Decision
options.body: Resolve the sandbox PTY warning/error policy first, then revisit whether a global PTY default should be allowed.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Opt-In
recommendation.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` with default `false`, per-call override precedence, direct/gateway coverage, docs/help, regression tests, and sandbox warning coordination.
